sample_unit: survey respondents (84 patients with axSpA and 26 rheumatologists); LLM responses to patient-identified concerns evaluated by 2 raters

links.outcome: Rate of safety disclaimers in LLM responses
links.effect: Disclaimer rates were GPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 100% and Kimi k1.5 88%; safety generally high, but hallucinations remain a critical barrier.
links.quote: GPT-4.0 and Kimi k1.5 demonstrated superior overall readability; safety remained generally high (disclaimer rates: GPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 100%; Kimi k1.5 88%).

unlisted_practices: Delphi consensus process to develop a patient-centered needs assessment questionnaire
Comparing clinician and patient priorities to customize patient education

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, readability, and safety disclaimers of multiple LLMs in answering patient-centered questions about axial spondyloarthritis without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice intervention.
